reason: Shaded areas under the normal curve show why the conditional probability divides by P(accepted), and how an inverse-normal value fixes k.

scenes.title: Conditional probability as a fraction of the accepted region
scenes.purpose: See that, given acceptance, the sample space shrinks to 460 to 480, so the answer is the small shaded area divided by the whole accepted area.

steps.text: The blue region is the accepted band $460 < R < 480$. Its area is $0.9044\ldots$, which is the denominator. This is the first M1.
The orange region is $475 < R < 480$, with area $0.1545\ldots$. It is the numerator, because you only count accepted resistors above $475$. This is the second M1.

The answer is the orange area as a fraction of the accepted area: $\frac{0.154538}{0.904419} \approx 0.171$, the A1. Drag $c$ down towards $460$ and the fraction heads towards $1$. Dividing by $\mathrm{P}(R>475)$ or not dividing at all would give a different number.

guide.what_you_see: The bell curve for the resistance $R \sim \mathrm{N}(470, 6^2)$ of a Line A resistor, with the accepted band from $460$ to $480$ ohms shaded blue and a smaller orange slice inside it that starts at the slider value $c$.

legend.meaning: The normal density curve of $R$, with mean $470$ and standard deviation $6$, from the question.
The blue region under the curve between $460$ and $480$: the probability that the tester accepts a resistor, $\mathrm{P}(460 < R < 480)\approx 0.9044$.
The orange region under the curve from $c$ to $480$: the accepted resistors with resistance above $c$. At $c=475$ it is $\mathrm{P}(475 < R < 480)\approx 0.1545$.
Vertical line at $R=460$, the lower acceptance limit.
Vertical line at $R=480$, the upper acceptance limit.

interact.do: Start at $c=475$, the value in the question. Then drag the slider down towards $460$ and back up towards $479$.
interact.watch: The orange region grows as $c$ decreases and shrinks as $c$ increases. At $c=475$ its area is $0.1545\ldots$, which is about $0.171$ of the blue area. As $c$ approaches $460$ the orange region fills the blue one, so the fraction tends to $1$.

question_link.text: The blue region $A$ is the probability of acceptance, which is the denominator of the conditional probability and earns the first M1. The orange region $U$ at $c=475$ is $\mathrm{P}(475 < R < 480)$, the numerator for the second M1. Their ratio $\frac{0.1545\ldots}{0.9044\ldots}\approx 0.171$ is the A1 answer.

read_off: 'P(accepted)' is the blue area, $\mathrm{P}(460 < R < 480)$. It stays fixed at about $0.9044$ and is the denominator.
'P(c < R < 480)' is the orange area. At $c=475$ it reads about $0.1545$, the numerator. Divide it by the 'P(accepted)' reading to get the answer, about $0.171$.

scenes.title: Sliding k until the lower tail is 0.075
scenes.purpose: See that k is the point where the area to its left is 0.075, which lies below the mean so its z-value is negative.

steps.text: The expected count $150$ out of $2000$ means $\mathrm{P}(R<k)=0.075$. The shaded area to the left of $k$ must equal $0.075$. This is the M1.

Drag $k$ to the left of the mean at $470$ until the area reads $0.075$. The standardised value there is $z=-1.4395$, negative because $k$ is below the mean. This is the B1. Moving $k$ to the right of $470$ would give a positive $z$ and an area above $0.5$.

interact.do: Drag the slider $k$ between $452$ and $480$, starting at $468$ and moving it left towards about $461$.
interact.watch: The shaded area to the left of the line at $k$ shrinks as $k$ moves left. At $k=461.4$ the area reads about $0.075$ and $z$ reads about $-1.44$. Moving $k$ past $470$ makes $z$ positive and the area rise above $0.5$.

legend.meaning: The bell-shaped density curve of $R\sim\mathrm{N}(470, 6^2)$, the resistance of a resistor from Line A, centred on $470$.
The shaded area under the curve to the left of $k$, which is the probability $\mathrm{P}(R<k)$.
The vertical line at $x=k$, the value you are trying to find.
The grey vertical line at the mean $470$, which marks where $z=0$.

question_link.text: The shaded area $L$ is $\mathrm{P}(R<k)$, which must equal $\frac{150}{2000}=0.075$ (the M1). The $z$ reading at that position is the negative value $-1.4395$ (the B1), and the line at $k$ then sits at $470-6\times1.4395\approx461.4$ (the A1).

read_off: The label 'P(R < k)' is the shaded area to the left of $k$, which is the probability that a resistor has resistance below $k$ ohms. You want it to equal $0.075$.
The label 'z = (k - 470)/6' is the standardised value of $k$, the number of standard deviations $k$ lies from the mean $470$. It is negative when $k<470$, and you want about $-1.4395$.
guide.what_you_see: The normal curve for the resistance $R\\sim\\mathrm{N}(470, 6^2)$ of a Line A resistor, with the area to the left of a movable line at $k$ shaded. A grey line marks the mean $470$.
